Subject: Legal assessment — TheraHealth redlines (summary)

Team / Jenna —

I reviewed the attached redlines and ran a short risk/mitigation analysis. Summary of key points and recommended positions:

- Liability cap: Removing the cap entirely exposes Redwood to unlimited exposure tied to an event. Our standard practice is to tie the cap to a multiple of subscription fees (e.g., 12 months) or a fixed ceiling (we typically push toward $500k for mid-market).
- Indemnity: The proposed broad indemnity for all third-party claims is overbroad. We can accept indemnity for data breaches caused by Redwood’s negligence but need carve-outs for third-party components and downstream claims.
- Warranty: 24-month warranty with SLA credits is excessive. Recommend limiting warranty remedies to 12 months, but we can offer an 18-month warranty for an additional service credit schedule and narrower scope (software defects only, not integration or customer misuse).
- Discount: A 30% first-year credit is outside standard delegated discounts. Sales can typically approve up to 15% without execs; anything >20% requires VP signoff.

Proposed alternative (legal-friendly):
- Cap: $500,000 aggregate liability or 12 months of fees, whichever is higher, except for gross negligence or willful misconduct where we accept a higher standard.
- Indemnity: Redwood indemnifies for Redwood-originated data breaches and IP infringement; exclude third-party integrations and customer-controlled configurations.
- Warranty: 18 months limited warranty for defects; SLA credits capped at defined percentages tied to incident severity.
- Discount: Recommend offering 20% first-year discount as a compromise.

If Sales wants to keep negotiating commercial levers (longer term commitment, annual upfront payment, or reference customer commitments), we can trade those for the additional concession.

I’ve attached a short legal memo and a redline showing the alternate language: risk_analysis_legal_memo.pdf, TheraHealth_redlines_v3.docx.

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Escalation: Exec decision needed on liability cap & discount for TheraHealth (DL-2027-1198)

Vivek / Laura —

Looping you both for an executive decision. Background: TheraHealth is requesting elimination of the liability cap, a 24-month warranty with broad SLA remedies, and a 30% first-year discount. Legal (Marissa) recommends a compromise: $500k cap (or 12 months fees), indemnity limited to Redwood-originated data breaches, 18-month limited warranty, and a 20% first-year discount as the maximum concession without board signoff.

Commercial considerations: this is a strategic POC for a large prospective channel partner with potential expansion into multiple hospitals. They have strong reference value and fast procurement pressure (ask to close by 9/30). Sales indicates we can get commitment to a 2-year minimum term and an upfront annual payment if we move to the 20% discount.

Recommendation (Evelyn): Approve the legal compromise — accept cap at $500k or 12 months of fees, indemnity narrowed per legal memo, warranty extended to 18 months with defined SLA credits, and authorize a 20% first-year discount contingent on a 2-year minimum term + upfront payment. If you prefer to keep commercial upside, alternatively authorize a final escalation to CEO for the full 30% and any cap removal.

Please reply with ONE of the following: APPROVE (as recommended), APPROVE + CEO ESCALATE (authorize me to take the 30% and cap removal to the CEO), or REJECT (I will inform the customer and propose the standard position). Time is tight — Jenna has asked for a decision by EOD 2027-09-17.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
